column3: Direct parallel: following what angers God and disliking His pleasure results in voided deeds.
Blessing and peace on the Prophet add no clear link to the stated cause of voided deeds.
Adds faith-disbelief as a distinct condition under which a deed becomes void.
Adds the concrete response of promising obedience to those who dislike what God sent down.
Nearby disclosure of inward states through speech offers only an indirect diagnostic parallel.
Adds a setting where declared disbelief accompanies voided deeds and lasting punishment.
Contrast boundary: faithlessness and hostile conduct precede voided deeds, without specifying the focus response.
Livestock beauty has no material bearing on the focus ayah.
Adds rejection, obstruction, and opposition after guidance as another route to voided deeds.
Opposition to God and the Messenger adds a broad rebellion context but no voiding mechanism.
Provides the inverse trajectory: guidance increases for those rightly guided.
Adds association with God as a separate stated condition that voids prior works.
Confirms worldly and final loss of deeds but adds little cause beyond the direct parallels.
Nearby testing of striving and patience supplies a limited context for deeds being examined.
Truth being established despite criminals' dislike parallels aversion but not the consequence for works.
Adds exposed claims of allegiance followed by voided deeds and loss.
God's invalidation of corrupt work is an outcome analogy, not the focus's stated cause.
Names the revelation as a descent from the Mighty, Merciful, without showing its reception.
Adds a response to a sent surah: turning away, followed by diverted hearts.
Nearby knowledge of God and seeking forgiveness offer a positive counterpoint only.
Contrast boundary: denial of signs and the meeting yields weightless deeds, but does not positively route the focus reading.
Adds ignorance of the limits of what God sent down within disbelief and hypocrisy.
Provision and later disagreement after knowledge add no focused link.
Identifies a descent from the Lord of the worlds but adds no response to it.
Adds an observable refusal: hypocrites are called to what God sent down and turn away.
Immediate context: unbelief is followed by ruin and the loss of deeds.
Adds unwilling worship and spending, with disbelief causing offerings not to be accepted.
The assurance that righteous exertion is recorded is only a positive counterpoint.
Nearby contrast between believing righteous action and unbelieving consumption adds little to the causal statement.
Sets the sent guidance and true religion against the dislike of associators.
Adds an unauthorized reshaping of God-given provision as a response to what He has sent.
Distinguishes outward submission from faith entering hearts, while obedience preserves deeds.
Contrast boundary: worldly manufacture is voided, but the route is not positive evidence for the focus.
Adds refusal to follow what God sent down in favor of inherited practice.
Nearby admission to Paradise adds no explanatory link to aversion and voided deeds.
Establishes that clear signs are sent down and that God guides whom He wills.
Directly parallels the response of disliking truth after it has been brought.
Immediate directive: obey God and the Messenger and do not nullify your deeds.
Affirms the Quran's descent, but its paired V12 contrast remains boundary evidence.
Contrasts invented religious names with authority God has not sent down and commands exclusive worship.
Livestock creation and benefit do not clarify the focus ayah.
A terse reference to a descent upon dividers supplies insufficient focused context.
Truth's establishment despite criminals' dislike repeats the aversion pattern without a deeds result.
Nearby contrast of divine protection for believers adds only a broad outcome frame.
The descent of rain and plant growth is unrelated to the response to revelation.
Commands sincere religion for God despite the dislike of disbelievers, giving an opposed response pattern.
Adds the contrast between evidence from God and evil action beautified by desire.
Names the Creator as the source of descent but gives no reception or consequence.
Immediate opening parallel: unbelief and blocking God's way make deeds go astray.
The descent of rain for drinking and pasture is not relevant here.
Adds a separate conditional cause for voided work; its V12 contrast link is boundary evidence only.
Oaths used as a shield and obstruction from God's way add a general hostile practice.
Nearby faith and mindfulness receiving reward form only a broad positive contrast.
Objection to the Messenger's ordinary life and demand for an angel is a remote rejection analogy.
Nearby curse, deafness, and blindness extend the consequences of turning away only indirectly.
Immediate inverse: faith in what was sent down to Muhammad brings reform rather than loss.
Adds an inversion in which people assign God what they themselves dislike and speak falsely.
Adds reversal after professed faith, followed by a sealed heart and lack of understanding.
Return and divine witness to actions do not clarify the stated cause.
The Quran's descent on the Night of Decree adds source context only.
Opposition to God and His Messenger adds a general rebellion consequence.
Nearby avarice exposing inner rancor offers an indirect inward-disposition parallel.
Adds explicit denial that the Most Merciful sent anything, alongside accusation of lying.
Different ranks before God and His sight of deeds are too general to add here.
Nearby warning of the Hour adds no focused account of voided deeds.
Identifies the revelation's merciful source but not acceptance or rejection.
Adds a command to judge by what God sent down, with refusal characterized as deviation.
Pharaoh's wealth and hardened hearts do not add a direct link.
States that the Quran was not sent to cause distress, a limited purpose counterpoint.
Misplaced fear and lack of understanding offer only an indirect inner-state parallel.
Nearby turning away and replacement extend a consequence of refusal without the revelation link.
A sent and required surah with clear signs establishes form but not the focus response.
False confidence about punishment does not materially explain the focus ayah.
Defines genuine believers through certainty and striving, as a broad inverse profile.
Clear signs sent down and denied by deviants provide a general reception contrast.
Messengers bringing clear proofs and being rejected adds a generic historical parallel.
Immediate context adds apostasy after guidance and deceptive encouragement.
God sent down the Book and protects the righteous, a limited positive counterpoint.
Adds preference for worldly life over the Hereafter as an inward preference opposed to guidance.
Nearby assurance that deeds will not be diminished supplies a positive contrast only.
What is evil is disliked by the Lord, but this is not about what He sent down.
Adds judging by what God sent down versus desires and the consequence of turning away.
Benefits and transport from livestock do not contribute to the focus reading.
Repeats the inherited-practice refusal to follow what God sent down, after the earlier stronger parallel.
Disbelief in God and the Messenger explains lack of forgiveness but not voided deeds specifically.
Nearby assurance that those killed in God's way will not have deeds lost gives a marked countercase.
A hypothetical descent to non-Arabs does not develop acceptance or rejection.
Adds active resistance to God's light despite disbelievers' dislike, with divine completion.
Livestock provision and warning against Satan's steps add no focused connection.
Presents a heard book as confirming and guiding, a recognition-side counterpoint.
Adds arrogance, denial of signs, and choosing error over right guidance as a reception pattern.
Adds association without revealed authority and speaking about God without knowledge.
Ritual and charitable commands concern good works but do not explain their nullification here.
Rain reviving the earth is not a relevant link to the focus ayah.
Distinguishes inward mindfulness from outward ritual material, an indirect deeds-value parallel.
Winds and rainwater provide no focused evidence.
Knowledge of actions alone adds no link to the cause of their loss.
Adds objection to the Quran being sent to an unexpected recipient, a distinct form of rejection.
The reality of dispute among the people of Fire is unrelated.
The Quran's gradual, divided descent adds process context only.
Directly states that turning back from faith and dying in disbelief voids one's deeds.
Adds a concrete way acts are invalidated: charity spoiled by reminders, injury, and display.
Adds disbelief in a confirming Book after it comes, a direct rejection-of-revelation pattern.
Explicitly frames disbelief in what God sent down as a wrongful chosen exchange.
Adds selective acceptance: believing an earlier sending while rejecting what God sent down afterward.
Adds non-acceptance of a religion other than submission to God and final loss.
Adds opposition to the Messenger and departure from the believers' way after guidance is clear.
Links what is sent down to the Messenger with increased rebellion and disbelief among rejecters.
Directly repeats refusal of what God sent down in favor of ancestral practice.
Commands following what has been sent down from the Lord rather than other allies.
Directly joins denial of signs and the Hereafter with voided deeds.
Adds spending to obstruct God's way, ending in regret and defeat.
Adds mocking God, His signs, and His Messenger as a decisive rejection response.
Explicitly identifies disbelief after professed faith, adding the reversal dimension.
Directly states that prior peoples' deeds became void in this world and the Hereafter.
Adds a sent surah that exposes hypocritical requests to be excused from commitment.
Shows divergent reception of a sent surah: faith increases for some while sickness increases for others.
Adds demand to replace or alter the recited Quran rather than receive it as sent.
Adds parties who deny part of what has been sent down amid the command to worship God alone.
Adds rejection of an Arabic judgment sent down and the warning against following desires after knowledge.
Provides the image of works reduced to scattered ashes under a destructive wind.
Records the dismissive answer to what the Lord has sent down: inherited tales.
Introduces those most lost with respect to their works.
Explains that their striving is lost while they suppose they are doing well.
Adds unstable, conditional worship that loses both this world and the Hereafter.
Adds an outcome parallel in which accumulated deeds are made scattered dust.
Explicitly refuses belief in this Quran and what came before it.
Adds organized refusal of the Quran: do not listen to it and drown it out.
Adds the response to clear verses when recited: calling the truth manifest sorcery.
Immediate context contrasts following falsehood with believers following truth sent down from their Lord.
Immediate context adds listening without comprehension, sealed hearts, and following desires.
Immediate context adds the reaction of diseased hearts when a decisive surah is sent down.
Immediate context asks whether they will contemplate the Quran or remain behind locked hearts.
Immediate context makes hidden rancor in diseased hearts relevant to outward response.
Immediate context joins disbelief and obstruction from God's way after the Messenger's message.
Directly warns that a mode of address to the Messenger can nullify deeds without awareness.
